target.title: fix(sqlite): serialize offline maintenance with gateway
target.body:
Related: #101290

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could start destructive SQLite maintenance while a Gateway was starting or still owned the same state directory, allowing compaction, import, recovery, or restore to race live database use. It also fixes shared-state compaction failing after ordinary CLI startup had already opened the state database for config-health observation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway startup and destructive doctor maintenance now share canonical state-directory ownership, with process identity checks and a crash-safe SQLite coordinator that serializes stale-lock reclamation. Shared-state compaction bypasses pre-command config-health observation so it acquires exclusive ownership before opening the database; normal doctor behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

SQLite snapshot, compaction, import, recovery, and restore operations now fail closed while a Gateway or peer maintenance command owns the state directory, recover safely after an owner crash, and avoid stale-lock replacement races. Operators can compact an offline shared state database through the normal CLI and retain byte-identical verified restore behavior.

## Evidence

- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- AWS Linux x64 focused lock/CLI suite: 87 tests passed (`run_c7c1c6e704cb`).
- AWS native Windows x64 focused lock/CLI suite: 86 passed, 1 expected symlink skip (`run_4e3d36640438`).
- Linux crash/high-I/O maintenance drill: live snapshot verified; active compaction refused; SIGKILL lock reclaimed; 99,409,920 bytes reclaimed from a 100,642,816-byte database; post-VACUUM snapshot restored byte-identically; quick/integrity/FK checks passed; unexpected unique index rejected without changing database bytes (`run_7cf4509aff48`).
- Cross-platform scenario proof also passed on macOS arm64, Linux x64, Docker Debian and Alpine/musl, AWS Graviton arm64, Apple VM arm64, WSL2 x64, native Windows x64, and ARM32 QEMU.
- Path-scoped hosted changed gate passed formatting, dependency/API guards, core production typecheck, and reached core test typecheck; the sparse remote mirror then lacked unrelated tracked `ui/config/control-ui-chunking.ts`. Repo-native prepare is the authoritative full-check gate.
